issues.explanation: In this poetic context, 转头 is a lexicalized expression meaning “in an instant”; splitting it into 转 and 头 encourages an incorrect literal reading.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge 转头 as one word with meaning “in an instant; in the blink of an eye.”

issues.explanation: 干政 is a standard word meaning “to interfere in government/politics.” Splitting it into 干 and 政 hides the useful lexical item in 宦官干政.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge 干政 as one word, meaning “to interfere in government/politics.”

issues.explanation: 结党 is a standard word meaning “to form a faction/clique.” Splitting it into 结 and 党 obscures the local meaning.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge 结党 as one word, meaning “to form a faction/clique.”

issues.explanation: 南华老仙 is a character’s fixed appellation/name in this passage. Splitting it into 南华 and 老仙 fails to keep the personal designation together.
issues.suggested_fix: Use one name segment 南华老仙, with meaning “Nanhua Old Immortal.”

issues.explanation: 天公将军 is a formal title, not an ordinary combination of the separate words “heaven” and “general.” The current split obscures the title’s localized meaning.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge 天公将军 as one title/name segment, meaning “Heavenly General.”

issues.explanation: 地公将军 is a formal title parallel to 天公将军 and 人公将军. Splitting it obscures the fixed title and produces an awkward literal gloss.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge 地公将军 as one title/name segment, meaning “Earthly General.”

issues.explanation: 人公将军 is a formal title parallel to 天公将军 and 地公将军. Splitting it obscures the fixed title and produces an awkward literal gloss.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge 人公将军 as one title/name segment, meaning “Human General.”
